findings.title: The disclosure becomes public proof
findings.claim: The divinely caused disclosure of the sleepers turns the promise and the Hour from an asserted future into publicly encountered proof, while remaining bounded by the promise itself.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins disclosure, intended knowing, the God-owned promise, and its truth; the surrounding awakening and truthful-report context supplies a completed path from hidden preservation to public evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The event is newly legible as evidence that can be encountered and known, not only as an isolated assertion about what will come.
findings.containment: The finding deepens the ordinary report that people were made aware of the sleepers; it does not claim that the mosque or every public response proves more than the cited promise and Hour.

findings.title: Proof closes one question and opens another
findings.claim: The focus settles the promise’s truth while leaving narration, counting, and claims about the sleepers open to public dispute under the Lord’s superior knowledge.
findings.mechanism: The context pairs speech without knowledge with later conjectural counting and dispute; the focus joins public speech to the declaration that their Lord knows them best, distinguishing warranted knowledge of the promise from exhaustive possession of the persons.
findings.reader_payoff: Discovery no longer appears to end uncertainty altogether: it yields a specific knowledge while the human struggle to narrate and count the sleepers continues.
findings.containment: The focus’s purpose clause still gives the public a real knowledge of the promise and Hour; the later counting may be a separate instruction rather than one continuous dispute, so the linkage is qualified.

findings.title: Human institution remains inside divine rule
findings.claim: The focus’s true promise stands within a contrast between contingent human institution and unshared divine control of future time and judgment.
findings.mechanism: The context subordinates human claims about tomorrow to divine willing, states a long duration while returning its knowledge to God, and denies any partner in judgment; the focus’s promise and human control over the affair therefore occupy different planes.
findings.reader_payoff: The mosque proposal can be seen as a consequential human act without being confused with the certainty or timing of the divine promise.
findings.containment: The closing judgment may govern revelation generally rather than directly evaluate the mosque decision; the finding preserves that qualification and the focus’s plain institutional proposal.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies conditional futurity, duration, divine knowledge, unshared judgment, and focus returns, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and the final comparison is inferential.
